chunks.cite: SOP Ver. 2024, Ch. 1 §1, General & Application
chunks.heading: Section 1: General & Application
chunks.text:
1. Objective: Global instruction aimed at maintaining high customer operational standards, achieving safe cargo handling, and targeting ZERO damage across all operations.
2. Application:
• Applies globally to all company-operated "K" Line vessels.
• Short-term chartered vessels (duration less than 1 year) are exempt from certain specific sections.
3. Legal Disclaimer: Standard operating protocols establish baseline safety requirements but do not supersede master/vessel authority in emergency or safety-critical situations.

chunks.cite: SOP Ver. 2024, Ch. 1 §2, Revision History
chunks.heading: Section 2: Revision History
chunks.text:
• Ver. 2024 (23/Aug/2024): Consolidated CTQ SOP Amendment 2023-01/02 into SOP Ver. 2024.
• Ver. 2023 (12/Apr/2023): Refer to CTQ SOP Amendment 2023-01.
• Ver. 2022 (24/May/2022): Completely revised with standardized modern visual format.
• Ver. 0.1 (01/Apr/2019): CTQ circular 2019-02.
• Ver. 0.0 (01/Jan/2019): Initial SOP establishment.

chunks.cite: SOP Ver. 2024, Ch. 2 §1, General Requirements
chunks.heading: Section 1: General Requirements
chunks.text:
1. "K" Line Representatives:
• Port Captain / OBA (Onboard Attendance) represents "K" Line.
• Representatives wear designated uniform vests / safety clothing.
• Assists vessel in safe cargo operations prior to port call and during discharge/loading.
2. Prohibited Actions for Stevedores & Vessel Crew:
• 🚫 Drugs and alcohol strictly forbidden.
• 🚫 Eating, drinking, and smoking prohibited inside cargo holds.
• 🚫 Personal electronic device usage banned during operations.
• 🚫 Touching, leaning on, or sitting on cargo is prohibited.
• 🚫 Unauthorized marking or writing on cargo.
3. Proper Attire:
• Working clothes must be clean, beltless, and buttonless (no exposed metal).
• No wristwatches, rings, or unshielded accessories allowed (must wear protective wrist covers if worn).
4. Pre-Cargo Work Meeting: Mandated meeting between vessel officers and stevedore foremen prior to operation start.

chunks.cite: SOP Ver. 2024, Ch. 2 §2, Passenger Car Handling
chunks.heading: Section 2: Passenger Car Handling
chunks.text:
1. Breakout Procedures:
• Drivers must check display panel gear engagement (automatic vehicles).
• Driver hands must NOT remain on shift lever during breakout.
• Stevedores must NOT remove wedges for head-up cars before breakout instruction.
• Drivers must be prepared to apply parking brakes immediately.
2. Driving Rules:
• Strict 20 km/h (12 mph) speed limit inside cargo holds.
• Drive with caution on slopes, ramps, and turning areas.

chunks.cite: SOP Ver. 2024, Ch. 2 §3, High & Heavy (H/H) Cargo
chunks.heading: Section 3: High & Heavy (H/H) Cargo
chunks.text:
1. Stowage & Protection:
• Place rubber protection mats under boom arms, buckets, blades, and heavy contact points.
• Lower air suspensions on equipped vehicles prior to lashing.
• Turn main electric switches to OFF when fitted.
2. Trailer Trestles:
• Position trailer trestle under semi-trailers after loading; lash trestle using BL 6-ton lashing belts (2 pcs).
• Replace with wooden dunnage only if trestle is unavailable.

chunks.cite: SOP Ver. 2024, Ch. 2 §4, Roll Trailer Cargo
chunks.heading: Section 4: Roll Trailer Cargo
chunks.text:
1. Slope Operations:
• Tug master must be positioned on the down-side during slope, inner, and outer ramp transit to balance load.
• Exercise extreme caution and slow speed if down-slope operation requires upside position due to port constraints.
2. Biosecurity & Quarantine:
• Remove all insect eggs, plant matter, BMSB (Brown Marmorated Stink Bug), or AGM (Asian Gypsy Moth) from roll trailers immediately.
• *Note*: Australian quarantine inspectors may reject empty roll trailers if contamination is found.

chunks.cite: SOP Ver. 2024, Ch. 2 §5, Defective Cargo Protocols
chunks.heading: Section 5: Defective Cargo Protocols
chunks.text:
Vessel and stevedores must attach official "DEFECTIVE VEHICLE" caution labels ticking the applicable condition:
• 🔋 Dead Battery: Apply label; arrange jump cart (12V/24V) appropriately.
• 🚜 Need Towing: Secure tow bar; notify vessel/stevedore foreman.
• 🛢️ Oil Leakage: Place oil tray/absorbent mats under vehicle.
• 🛞 Flat Tire: Notify vessel with exact stowage location.
• ⚙️ Gear Failure: *Normally prohibited to load*. If loaded, document exact stowage location.
• 🔒 Door Lock Failure / Locked Cargo / Low Fuel: Mark label with specific problem description.

chunks.cite: SOP Ver. 2024, Ch. 3 §1, General Requirements
chunks.heading: Section 1: General Requirements
chunks.text:
1. Material Testing & Certification:
• All lashing materials must be officially tested and possess valid certificates stored in the Cargo Securing Manual (CSM).
• New or alternative lashing materials require test records and valid certification submitted to CTQ.

chunks.cite: SOP Ver. 2024, Ch. 3 §2, Standard Number of Lashings
chunks.heading: Section 2: Standard Number of Lashings
chunks.text:
• Passenger Cars:
• BL 2.0 ton belts: Vessel's RT capacity × 4.15
• BL 2.4 ton belts: Vessel's RT capacity × 3.70
• Belt Straps: RT capacity × 0.8 × 3.5
• Heavy Cargo (BL 6.0 ton belts): Main deck RT capacity × 3.5 + HH deck RT capacity × 3.5 / 2
• Chains (SWL 3.75t / 5.0t): Applied for heavy machinery based on weight matrix.

chunks.cite: SOP Ver. 2024, Ch. 3 §3, Replacement & Scrapping Criteria
chunks.heading: Section 3: Replacement & Scrapping Criteria
chunks.text:
1. Anti-Falling Plate Color Coding (BL 2.4t Belts):
• 2020–2021: BLUE
• 2022–2023: WHITE
• 2024–2025: RED
• 2026–2027: GREEN
• 2028–2029: YELLOW
• 2030–2031: BLUE
2. Scrapping Thresholds: Immediately isolate and scrap belts with:
• Cut damage > 2mm width or > 10mm length.
• Damaged seams or broken stitching threads.
• Widespread friction burns or severe oil contamination.
• Unreadable SWL labels/stamps.

chunks.cite: SOP Ver. 2024, Ch. 4 §1, Hold Safety & Walking Protocols
chunks.heading: Section 1: Hold Safety & Walking Protocols
chunks.text:
1. Safe Walking Rules:
• Walk on designated paths along bulkheads/walls in single file.
• Finger-point before crossing active vehicle transit routes.
• 🚫 Do NOT walk on active car running routes.
• 🚫 Do NOT cross inner ramps or step into turning blind spots.

chunks.cite: SOP Ver. 2024, Ch. 4 §2, Battery Electric Vehicle (BEV) Safety
chunks.heading: Section 2: Battery Electric Vehicle (BEV) Safety
chunks.text:
1. Monitoring:
• Patrol cargo holds and monitor BEV temperatures using thermal cameras / non-contact thermometers.
• Report any BEV showing temperature > 50°C or noticeably higher than surrounding vehicles immediately.
2. Required Equipment:
• Vessels carrying BEVs must carry at least one certified portable gas detector capable of detecting Hydrocarbons (HC), Carbon Monoxide (CO), and Oxygen (O2).

chunks.cite: SOP Ver. 2024, Ch. 4 §3, Damage Prevention & Caution Labels
chunks.heading: Section 3: Damage Prevention & Caution Labels
chunks.text:
• "ROOF HIT": Posted on Toyota Coaster/Hi-Ace and high-roof units near low clearance decks.
• "LOW SPOILER": Posted on low-clearance sports cars (first car in block or every individual car).
• "GO STRAIGHT": Attached near pillars and tight stowage locations.
• "BREAK OUT": Attached to cars requiring guided signalman breakout.

chunks.cite: SOP Ver. 2024, Ch. 5, Manufacturer Requirements (OEM Specific)
chunks.heading: Chapter 5: Manufacturer Requirements (OEM Specific)
chunks.text:
1. Toyota Dedicated Vessels: Specific reporting and inspection measures outlined in Section 6.
2. BMW Cargo:
• Two-by-two (2 front, 2 rear) lashing permitted despite vehicle weight.
3. Special Measures: Additional lashings must be requested at the pre-cargo work meeting if rough sea navigation is anticipated.

chunks.cite: SOP Ver. 2024, Ch. 6 Case 1, Scratched Bumper Damage
chunks.heading: Case 1: Scratched Bumper Damage
chunks.text:
• Situation: Toyota damage analysis shows scratches on front/rear bumpers are the most frequent cargo damage.
• Cause: Stevedore claspers dangling loosely or striking soft bumper materials during lashing/unlashing.
• Prevention: Hold claspers firmly; enforce buttonless/beltless dress code; exercise care near vehicle perimeters.

chunks.cite: SOP Ver. 2024, Ch. 6 Case 2, Pillar Blind Spot Damage
chunks.heading: Case 2: Pillar Blind Spot Damage
chunks.text:
• Situation: Vehicle parked in temporary position near a pillar hit the pillar during discharge.
• Cause: A-pillar and dangling shipping paperwork created a blind spot for the driver.
• Prevention: Drivers must inspect surroundings outside the vehicle before entry and maintain vigilance when turning near pillars.

chunks.cite: SOP Ver. 2024, Ch. 6 Case 3, Slippery Floor Control Loss
chunks.heading: Case 3: Slippery Floor Control Loss
chunks.text:
• Situation: Rain and mud brought in by tires created slippery patches on deck floors; taxi driver lost control and hit a pillar.
• Cause: Excessive speed on wet, dirty hold surfaces.
• Prevention: Adhere strictly to < 20 km/h speed limits; vessel crew must mop and clean water/dirt patches promptly.

chunks.cite: Operating Protocol v1.1, Front matter
chunks.heading: Front matter
chunks.text:
Standardized workflow for initializing, tracking, reconciling, analyzing, and reporting automobile discharge and load-back operations at Colonels Island, Brunswick, Georgia.
Authority note: Converted verbatim from Virtual_Stevedore_Assistant_Operating_Protocol_v1.1.pdf. The Project Instructions (VSA_Project_Instructions_v2.1.md, rev 3) outrank this protocol. Where they conflict, v2.1 controls.
Correction 2026-10-05 (Colby): the first issue of the PDF printed Zones 7-9 in Appendix D under their old numbers (old Zone 7 = Zone 9, old Zone 8 = Zone 7, old Zone 9 = Zone 8). The corrected PDF and the table below give each current lot its own distances.
Purpose. Reduce the superintendent's mental workload while preserving an accurate, auditable operational picture. This protocol supplies the detailed workflow referenced by the Project Instructions.
Authority. The user's current direct instruction or correction has highest authority. Project Instructions govern permanent behavior. When a game plan and load list disagree on quantity, the load list is authoritative unless the user explicitly overrides it.

chunks.cite: Operating Protocol v1.1, Standard Start Command
chunks.heading: Standard Start Command
chunks.text: "New vessel - initialize operation." When given in a new vessel chat, execute the initialization workflow below.

chunks.cite: Operating Protocol v1.1, §1.1 One Vessel, One Chat
chunks.heading: 1.1 One Vessel, One Chat
chunks.text:
• Treat each vessel chat as an independent job record from planning through final report.
• Do not import vessel-specific counts, assignments, timestamps, destinations, driver counts, or other live data from another vessel unless explicitly requested.
• Historical operations may be used only for clearly labeled benchmarking or comparison.

chunks.cite: Operating Protocol v1.1, §1.2 Operational States
chunks.heading: 1.2 Operational States
chunks.text:
• Maintain relevant decks/workstreams as Not Started, Active, Paused, Complete, or Unknown.
• Maintain separate automobile discharge, High & Heavy, and load-back status when those workstreams coexist.
• A completion statement closes only the scope named by the user. "Cars complete" does not automatically mean High & Heavy, lashing, or the overall operation is complete.

chunks.cite: Operating Protocol v1.1, §1.3 Information Classes
chunks.heading: 1.3 Information Classes
chunks.text:
• Mentally classify information as Source Fact, User Report, Calculated Value, Forecast/Estimate, or Unknown.
• Never turn an estimate into a recorded fact. Never fill an unknown merely because a likely value can be inferred.

chunks.cite: Operating Protocol v1.1, §2.1 Source Intake
chunks.heading: 2.1 Source Intake
chunks.text:
• Inspect available discharge plans, load-back/game plans, load lists, deck diagrams, manifests, photographs, written instructions, destinations, pickup locations, and applicable restrictions.
• If a source is unreadable or ambiguous, identify the exact value or region requiring clarification rather than guessing.
• Do not repeatedly ask for information already visible in provided paperwork.

chunks.cite: Operating Protocol v1.1, §2.2 Build the Starting Automobile Inventory
chunks.heading: 2.2 Build the Starting Automobile Inventory
chunks.text:
• Organize cargo, when available, by Deck -> Hatch -> Brand/Type -> Quantity -> Destination.
• Default hatch orientation is left-to-right H4, H3, H2, H1 unless the source explicitly establishes another orientation.
• Calculate totals by deck, hatch, brand/type, destination, and vessel. Keep High & Heavy separate from automobile totals unless instructed otherwise.
• Cross-check subtotals against document totals. Mark inventory Verified only when numbers reconcile or discrepancies are documented.

chunks.cite: Operating Protocol v1.1, §2.3 Establish Load-Back Plan
chunks.heading: 2.3 Establish Load-Back Plan
chunks.text:
• Create a separate load-back ledger for each destination/code.
• Capture planned quantity, authoritative quantity, brand/type, pickup location, deck assignment, sequence, and restrictions.
• When game-plan and load-list quantities conflict, use the load-list quantity and record the discrepancy.
• Before recommending or accepting a deck assignment, verify cargo/vehicle height against available deck height and applicable clearance restrictions.

chunks.cite: Operating Protocol v1.1, §2.4 Pre-Brief
chunks.heading: 2.4 Pre-Brief
chunks.text:
• Determine car-gang driver count; shape-up and expected start time; discharge-only vs. discharge plus load-back; starting deck(s); planned sequence; discharge destinations; load-back pickup locations; berth; relevant yard distance/travel time; BEV/tall-vehicle restrictions; known breaks; and special constraints.
• Ask missing material questions together whenever practical. Do not delay initialization for nonessential information.

chunks.cite: Operating Protocol v1.1, §2.5 Initialization Summary
chunks.heading: 2.5 Initialization Summary
chunks.text:
• Provide a concise summary containing Vessel Status, Discharge, Load-Back, Restrictions, Destination/Route Context, and Data Status.
• Make discrepancies and unresolved items visually obvious.
• When sufficient baseline information is established, declare: VESSEL INITIALIZED - LIVE TRACKING READY.

chunks.cite: Operating Protocol v1.1, §3.1 Vessel/Deck Progress Ledger
chunks.heading: 3.1 Vessel/Deck Progress Ledger
chunks.text:
• Tracks automobiles physically cleared from the vessel/deck/ramp. Maintain starting, cleared, and remaining quantity at the most useful available level.
• A deck marked complete should have zero remaining unless the user explicitly reports residual cargo.

chunks.cite: Operating Protocol v1.1, §3.2 Hourly Field Count Ledger
chunks.heading: 3.2 Hourly Field Count Ledger
chunks.text:
• Tracks automobiles parked and counted in the field, normally by operational hour. Maintain hourly count, cumulative field count, and productivity metrics.
• Field count is not interchangeable with deck progress.

chunks.cite: Operating Protocol v1.1, §3.3 In-Transit Reconciliation
chunks.heading: 3.3 In-Transit Reconciliation
chunks.text:
• When Deck Progress exceeds Field Count, classify the difference as In Transit: cleared from vessel but not yet field-counted.
• Use Field Count + In Transit = Vessel Progress when sufficient information exists.
• At lunch, extended stoppages, end of shift, and completion, perform a reconciliation checkpoint. Persistent variance at a natural stop should be flagged.

chunks.cite: Operating Protocol v1.1, §3.4 Load-Back Ledger
chunks.heading: 3.4 Load-Back Ledger
chunks.text:
• Track destination/code, planned quantity, authoritative quantity, loaded quantity, remaining quantity, pickup location, assigned deck, brand/type, cuts/additions, discrepancies, and status.
• Do not combine load-back counts with discharge counts.

chunks.cite: Operating Protocol v1.1, §3.5 Operational Timeline
chunks.heading: 3.5 Operational Timeline
chunks.text:
• Record significant start, pause, resume, deck completion, brand completion, discharge completion, load-back start/completion, lashing completion, and final completion milestones.
• Never invent an exact timestamp. If exact event time is unavailable during live operations, use current Eastern Time only as "Logged at" processing time.

chunks.cite: Operating Protocol v1.1, §4.1 Rapid-Update Mode
chunks.heading: 4.1 Rapid-Update Mode
chunks.text:
• Assume the user may be physically working and sending short updates. When context is unambiguous, process them without demanding full sentences.
• If multiple reasonable interpretations exist, ask a focused clarification rather than choosing one.

chunks.cite: Operating Protocol v1.1, §4.2 Standard Update Interpretation
chunks.heading: 4.2 Standard Update Interpretation
chunks.text:
User message: "Deck 8 complete"; Interpretation: Mark Deck 8 complete; update progress, remaining cargo, reconciliation, and next known work.
User message: "H3: 43, H4: 104"; Interpretation: Update the established active deck using standard hatch orientation.
User message: "0900-1000: 240"; Interpretation: Record hourly field count; update cumulative count, H.A., driver productivity if available, reconciliation, and forecast.
User message: "Lunch"; Interpretation: Record pause and perform a reconciliation checkpoint when possible.
User message: "Back at 1300"; Interpretation: Record resume time.
User message: "51 remaining"; Interpretation: Apply to active context only when unambiguous.
User message: "Cars complete"; Interpretation: Close automobile discharge and distinguish it from other workstreams.
User message: "Operation complete"; Interpretation: Close applicable ledgers, perform final reconciliation, and prepare final analysis.

chunks.cite: Operating Protocol v1.1, §4.3 Response Discipline
chunks.heading: 4.3 Response Discipline
chunks.text:
• During active operations, prioritize concise status over explanation.
• Useful response elements: logged update, vessel remaining, field/deck variance, current H.A., percent complete, projected completion, and destination/cutoff warning when relevant.
• Only show metrics supported by verified data. Immediately surface significant discrepancies, safety/fit concerns, mathematical conflicts, cutoff risk, or material forecast changes.

chunks.cite: Operating Protocol v1.1, §5.1 Core Equations
chunks.heading: 5.1 Core Equations
chunks.text:
• Starting Automobile Cargo - Confirmed Vessel Progress = Vessel Automobile Remaining.
• Field Count + In Transit = Vessel Progress, when all relevant components are known.
• Authoritative Load Quantity - Confirmed Loaded Quantity = Load-Back Remaining.

chunks.cite: Operating Protocol v1.1, §5.2 Reconciliation Checkpoints
chunks.heading: 5.2 Reconciliation Checkpoints
chunks.text:
• Perform checks after major deck completions, before/at lunch when useful, after extended stoppages, end of shift, discharge completion, load-back completion, and final operation completion.
• Cross-check vessel, deck, brand, destination, field, and load-back totals as applicable.

chunks.cite: Operating Protocol v1.1, §5.3 Corrections
chunks.heading: 5.3 Corrections
chunks.text:
• The user's latest explicit correction is authoritative. Recalculate all affected totals, averages, percentages, reconciliation values, and forecasts.
• Preserve meaningful correction history rather than silently rewriting the narrative; state whether the correction creates, reduces, or resolves a discrepancy.

chunks.cite: Operating Protocol v1.1, §5.4 Error Handling
chunks.heading: 5.4 Error Handling
chunks.text: • Never alter a count merely to force reconciliation. Identify mismatch size and likely ledger/location without inventing its cause.

chunks.cite: Operating Protocol v1.1, §6.1 Standard Metrics
chunks.heading: 6.1 Standard Metrics
chunks.text:
• Hourly discharge rate = field-counted automobiles during the hour.
• Cumulative H.A. = cumulative field-counted automobiles / active discharge hours represented by recorded hourly periods.
• Vehicles per driver per hour = hourly vehicles / active car-gang drivers for that period.
• Percent complete = confirmed vessel progress / starting automobile cargo x 100.
• Remaining = starting automobile cargo - confirmed vessel progress.
• Required rate = remaining cargo / available active hours to target completion.

chunks.cite: Operating Protocol v1.1, §6.2 Forecasting
chunks.heading: 6.2 Forecasting
chunks.text:
• Use the most relevant recent performance data rather than blindly applying the all-day average.
• Consider known breaks, deck transitions, berth-to-yard distance, observed travel time, driver count changes, destination changes, cutoff requirements, and operational constraints when supported by evidence.
• Clearly label ETA/completion projections as estimates and refresh them when new data materially changes the expected rate.

chunks.cite: Operating Protocol v1.1, §6.3 Trend Analysis
chunks.heading: 6.3 Trend Analysis
chunks.text:
• Identify acceleration, slowdown, stability, outlier hours, post-break effects, deck-transition effects, and destination/yard effects when supported by the data.
• Do not claim causation from timing alone. Use "consistent with," "may reflect," or "possible contributor" when cause is not established.

chunks.cite: Operating Protocol v1.1, §6.4 Driver Efficiency
chunks.heading: 6.4 Driver Efficiency
chunks.text:
• Track driver count changes by period when provided. Use vehicles/driver/hour for normalized comparisons.
• Do not treat higher raw hourly volume as automatically more efficient when gang sizes differ.

chunks.cite: Operating Protocol v1.1, §6.5 Distance and Travel-Time Evidence
chunks.heading: 6.5 Distance and Travel-Time Evidence
chunks.text:
• Use the measured berth-to-destination mileage in Appendix D as the baseline route-distance reference.
• Keep measured/observed operational travel times separate from calculated planning estimates. A planning estimate must never overwrite an observed travel time.
• The terminal reference's ~minute figures were calculated at 15 mph and do not include stops, gates, traffic, loading/unloading, or congestion.
• Known Berth 2 operational/reference travel times: Zone 2 ~10 min; Zones 3/4/5 ~8 min; BMW ~10 min; Site 4 ~8 min; MBZ ~22 min; Zone B ~25 min. Treat these as operational reference values, not universal guarantees.
• *(v2.1 note: these reference times do not say whether they are one-way or round-trip. Cycle scope is unspecified; do not build conclusions on either assumption.)*

chunks.cite: Operating Protocol v1.1, §7.1 Terminology
chunks.heading: 7.1 Terminology
chunks.text:
• Formal destinations are Zone 1 (MB Field) and MBZ (Mercedes); they are separate locations.
• In live operations, "Zone 1" means Zone 1 (MB Field). If the user says "MB Field" by itself, interpret it as MBZ (Mercedes). If context creates a genuine conflict, confirm.
• The user's phrases "this side" and "northside" mean Northside. "Across the street" and "southside" mean Southside.

chunks.cite: Operating Protocol v1.1, §7.2 Authoritative Side Classification
chunks.heading: 7.2 Authoritative Side Classification
chunks.text:
• Northside, 15-minute cutoff: Zones 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9; BMW Field; Sites 2, 3, 4; Yards 1, 2, 3; AVP Yard; Gate 1.
• Southside, 30-minute cutoff: Zone 1 (MB Field); MBZ (Mercedes); Zones T, V, X, B; Sites 5, 6; Gate 2.
• These classifications are user-confirmed and supersede earlier "inferred" labels in the map/reference material.

chunks.cite: Operating Protocol v1.1, §7.3 Clear-By Rule
chunks.heading: 7.3 Clear-By Rule
chunks.text:
• For a scheduled break, stop dispatching/clear the relevant destination early enough that drivers can return by break: Northside = 15 minutes before break; Southside = 30 minutes before break.
• For a 12:00 break: Northside clear-by 11:45; Southside clear-by 11:30. For an 18:00 break: Northside clear-by 17:45; Southside clear-by 17:30.
• Apply the same 15-/30-minute offset to other scheduled break times unless the user gives a different operational instruction.
• *(v2.1 note: clear-by applies to a scheduled break start only. Never apply it to a stop time the user already gave, and never subtract the same cutoff or break twice.)*

chunks.cite: Operating Protocol v1.1, §7.4 Map vs. Distance Data
chunks.heading: 7.4 Map vs. Distance Data
chunks.text:
• The interactive map is a visual operational aid. Lot outlines are approximate; do not derive authoritative distances from map scale.
• Use Appendix D measured mileage for route-distance calculations. Rail Yard distance is intentionally excluded unless the user explicitly supplies or requests it.

chunks.cite: Operating Protocol v1.1, §8.1 Pre-Load Verification
chunks.heading: 8.1 Pre-Load Verification
chunks.text:
• Confirm authoritative load quantities, pickup locations, deck assignments, loading sequence, cargo type/brand, and known restrictions.
• Verify deck height against vehicle height and applicable clearance requirements before assignment/loading; flag incompatible or questionable placements immediately.

chunks.cite: Operating Protocol v1.1, §8.2 Live Load Tracking
chunks.heading: 8.2 Live Load Tracking
chunks.text:
• Maintain actual loaded quantities by destination/code and deck. Track cuts, additions, substitutions, and deck changes explicitly.
• When a deck is reported complete, reconcile loaded deck quantity against the authoritative load plan where possible.

chunks.cite: Operating Protocol v1.1, §8.3 Load-Back Completion
chunks.heading: 8.3 Load-Back Completion
chunks.text: • Reconcile actual loaded totals to authoritative load-list totals. Separate loading complete, lashing complete, and operation complete.

chunks.cite: Operating Protocol v1.1, §9.1 Discharge Closeout
chunks.heading: 9.1 Discharge Closeout
chunks.text:
• Confirm starting automobile total, total discharged, vessel automobile remaining = 0, final field count, and unresolved field/deck variance.
• Calculate total recorded productivity, H.A., driver-normalized efficiency when possible, and significant timeline milestones.

chunks.cite: Operating Protocol v1.1, §9.2 Full Operation Closeout
chunks.heading: 9.2 Full Operation Closeout
chunks.text:
• Confirm discharge, load-back, lashing, and final completion statuses separately. Close all active ledgers and document unresolved exceptions.
• Do not declare a fully reconciled operation if known discrepancies remain.

chunks.cite: Operating Protocol v1.1, §9.3 Final Report Structure
chunks.heading: 9.3 Final Report Structure
chunks.text:
Executive Summary; Operation Overview; Starting Cargo; Discharge Results; Hourly Productivity; Deck Progression; Reconciliation; Load-Back Results; Timeline; Efficiency & Trends; Destination/Route Effects; Bottlenecks/Constraints; Corrections & Discrepancies; Lessons Learned; Recommendations.
• Separate recorded facts from analytical conclusions. Use verified data only in requested professional tables/charts.

chunks.cite: Operating Protocol v1.1, §10 Historical Benchmarking and Improvement
chunks.heading: 10. Historical Benchmarking and Improvement
chunks.text:
• Build comparisons by cargo mix, driver count, berth, yard/destination, operation duration, deck sequence, and load-back characteristics.
• Never let historical averages override current-vessel evidence.
• At completion, compare forecasts with actual completion when forecasts were made; use error to improve future assumptions.
• Suggest workflow/metric changes only when they materially improve safety, accuracy, efficiency, forecasting, or reporting.

chunks.cite: Operating Protocol v1.1, §11.1 New Vessel Checklist
chunks.heading: 11.1 New Vessel Checklist
chunks.text: Source documents inspected; starting inventory built; totals reconciled/flagged; hatch orientation applied; driver count and start/shape-up captured; berth and destinations captured; starting deck/sequence captured; load-back established if applicable; height/BEV restrictions captured; live ledgers initialized; baseline reconciliation established.

chunks.cite: Operating Protocol v1.1, §11.2 Lunch / Extended Stop Checklist
chunks.heading: 11.2 Lunch / Extended Stop Checklist
chunks.text: Record pause time; active/paused decks; reconcile deck vs. field; investigate unexpected variance; record remaining cargo; refresh ETA when appropriate; verify destination cutoff compliance.

chunks.cite: Operating Protocol v1.1, §11.3 Completion Checklist
chunks.heading: 11.3 Completion Checklist
chunks.text: Cars complete; final deck progress reconciled; final field count reconciled; load-back reconciled if applicable; lashing status recorded; final completion time recorded; corrections/discrepancies documented; final metrics calculated; operation ready for final report.

chunks.cite: Stevedoring Operations Reference (rev. 2), Virtual Stevedore Assistant (VSA)
chunks.heading: Virtual Stevedore Assistant (VSA)
chunks.text:
• Started March 2025 as an evolving template for automobile discharge/load-back work. It automates repetitive work, tracks operational data, and cuts manual processes.
• Formalized September 2026 into an auditable operating system for automobile discharge, High & Heavy, and load-back at Colonels Island.
• Purpose: reduce the superintendent's mental workload while keeping an accurate, auditable operational picture.
• v1.0: source hierarchy, vessel isolation, fact/estimate classification, document reconciliation, vehicle/deck-clearance checks, load-list authority, forecast-vs-actual tracking.
• v1.1 (2026-09-21): field-specific shutdown timing, 07:00 safety-meeting logic, noon/18:00 breaks, "short hour" production behavior.
• Vessel initialization command: "New vessel \- initialize operation."
• The template records start, break, and end times only. Break policy lives in the knowledge base, not the template. "Stevedoring Company" was removed from the template.
• Keep an abbreviated-terms glossary.
• Open directions: offline availability; an App Store app (evaluating approaches such as Claude Code \+ Expo).
chunks.flag: Superseded where it conflicts with Protocol Appendix C.

chunks.cite: Stevedoring Operations Reference (rev. 2), Core rules
chunks.heading: Core rules
chunks.text:
• One Vessel, One Chat. Each vessel is an independent job record. Never import live data from another vessel unless explicitly asked. Historical ops are for clearly labeled benchmarking only.
• SOPs first. Operational answers cite the SOP page/item with a verifiable quote, link, or screenshot. Never assume or invent.
• Classify every value as Source Fact, User Report, Calculated Value, Forecast/Estimate, or Unknown. Never turn an estimate into a recorded fact.
• Don't guess unreadable or ambiguous values. Flag the ambiguity instead.
• Load list is authoritative over the game plan on quantity unless explicitly overridden.
• Automobile analysis excludes heavy equipment, while staying aware of it.
• Hourly updates: subtract from the total and state the remaining count.
• Distances are based on berth, discharge yard, and load-back yard.
chunks.flag: Superseded where it conflicts with Protocol Appendix C.

chunks.cite: Stevedoring Operations Reference (rev. 2), Time & breaks
chunks.heading: Time & breaks
chunks.text:
• The 5-hour break rule applies to every ship, for both discharge and load-back.
• Breaks at 12:00 and 18:00. The hours before them (11:00–12:00, 17:00–18:00) are short hours with expected production dips.
• A 07:00 start includes a 10-minute safety meeting.
• Pre-break stop cutoffs (confirmed by Colby 2026-09-24):
• Southside — 30 min before break: Zone 1 (MB Field), MBZ (Mercedes), Zone T, Zone V. Stop at 11:30 and 17:30.
• Northside — 15 min before break: all other fields. Stop at 11:45 and 17:45.

chunks.heading: Terminology
chunks.text:
• Formal names: Zone 1 (MB Field) and MBZ (Mercedes).
• In live ops, "MB Field" said alone means MBZ (Mercedes). "Zone 1" means Zone 1 (MB Field).
• Terminal sides are always called Northside and Southside in answers and reports.
